SECTION B
Answer one question from this section.
We-ness
For a long time it was believed that in emergency situations an escaping crowd would panic.
Recent evidence has shown that most crowds do not panic. Instead they look to each other
for help and support. They believe that ‘we’ are all in it together. They develop ‘we-ness’.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have found out about crowd behaviour.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Evaluate what psychologists have found out about crowd behaviour.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Giving reasons for your answer, suggest what may be done to prevent panic in a crowd during
an emergency situation. 
How can we help?
In 2010 a major earthquake killed many thousands of people. There is not very much
psychologists can do to help with such natural disasters. We can be more helpful, however,
when trying to prevent a technological catastrophe.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have discovered about natural disaster and/or technological
catastrophe.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about natural disaster and/or technological
catastrophe.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Using your psychological knowledge, suggest ways in which psychologists could help people
after a disaster and/or catastrophe has happened.

• Chernobyl (1986): explosion and radioactivity released into the air at 1.24am
I would much rather work the morning shift!
